theory.intro: A **continuous uniform distribution** spreads probability evenly across an interval $[a,b]$, so its density is the constant $f(x)=\frac{1}{b-a}$. Every probability is then the area of a rectangle.
facts: $f(x)=\frac{1}{b-a}$ for $a\le x\le b$, and $f(x)=0$ for every other value of $x$.
$P(c\le X\le d)=\frac{d-c}{b-a}$, the width of the interval divided by the width of the whole support.
An interval running outside $[a,b]$ is cut back to the boundary, because $f(x)=0$ outside the support.
The mean sits at the midpoint of the support, $\mu=\frac{a+b}{2}$.
The variance is $\sigma^{2}=\frac{(b-a)^{2}}{12}$, so a wider support gives a larger spread.
steps: Find the width of the support, $b-a$.
Multiply the density by the width of the interval asked for.

development.solution_text:
$\frac{(b-1)^{2}}{12}=3$
$(b-1)^{2}=36$
$b-1=6$ or $b-1=-6$
$b=7$ or $b=-5$
$b=-5$ is rejected because $b$ must be greater than $a=1$.
$b=7$
